discussion_comments.comment_body: Changed in 5d243c5afd: on Windows the runner pins the root with the addon's `Process.fromPid` at spawn and calls `killTree()` on abort (the primitive `ptree` uses); POSIX keeps the process-group kill. Tested on Windows 11 / Git for Windows 2.56, and it is only a partial fix there: git runs hooks through MSYS `sh`, which forks via an extra stub process per command, and `Process.children()` does not list that stub even though its ppid is `sh`. So `killTree` stops `git`, `git.exe` and `sh`, but the hook's own commands keep running. `taskkill /T` misses the same branch, so `ptree` has the same gap. Catching them would need Job Object support in `pi-natives`, which I think belongs in its own PR. The abort itself still rejects immediately, so the repo lock is released.

Fixed in 9faee6924f: the signal is checked again right after `mkdtemp`, and nothing awaits between that check and registering the abort listener, so an abort can no longer slip into the gap. Not covered by a deterministic test (the abort would have to land inside that single await).

Fixed in 9faee6924f: only the last 64 KiB of each stream is read back (checked with a hook writing 200 KB: 65,536 bytes returned, final line intact). The temp files still grow while a hook writes, as its output would in a terminal; memory is what's bounded.

Fixed in f43cad40f4: the hook-file `stat` and the executable check are raced against the signal (the same `untilAborted` helper also covers the `git version` wait). New test: `fs.promises.stat` stalls for the hook file; aborting rejects with `AbortError`. It times out on the previous commit.

Fixed in f885e9889e: the hook's spawn path (output to files, own process group, group SIGKILL on abort; `killTree` on Windows) is now one helper, and `git version` runs through it as well, so an abort also kills whatever a wrapper started. The `abort also stops a hung git version check` test now asserts that the wrapper's child is gone after the abort, instead of only cleaning it up in `finally`; that assertion fails on the previous commit.

Fixed in f04f023312: the lookup is inverted. The git on `PATH` now always locates the hook (`git rev-parse --git-path hooks/post-checkout`, abortable, output capped), so wrapper and distribution config count as well as `-c` and environment overrides. This supersedes the environment comparisons described in earlier replies on this PR (`GIT_CONFIG*`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `HOME`/XDG), which are removed. The in-process lookup is only used when no git starts or gives a usable answer, so `/wt` still needs no git binary when there's no hook and reports an existing one as not run. New test: a `git` wrapper on `PATH` that exports its own `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` setting `core.hooksPath`; the hook runs. It fails on the previous commit when the developer has no global `core.hooksPath` of their own. The cost is one `git rev-parse` per new worktree, also when there is no hook.

Fixed in 97a72388d8: reading the probe output (`rev-parse`, `git version`) and the hook's captured output now races the signal too, like the hook-file `stat` and the capture directory. New test, for both the hook-path probe and the hook output: the read stalls, and the abort rejects with `AbortError`. On the previous commit both time out.

Fixed in 34307c58eb: the runner now pins the root at spawn and on abort calls `Process.killTree` (the primitive `ptree` uses). It snapshots the descendants by parent, then signals the root's process group, the descendants and the root, so a descendant that moved into its own session with `setsid` is reached as long as its parent is in the tree. A group kill afterwards still covers a root that had exited before it could be pinned. New test: the hook starts `setsid sh -c '…; exec sleep 30' &` and waits; after the abort the sleep is gone. On the previous commit it survives. A descendant that double-forks out and is reparented to init still escapes; catching that needs a subreaper like `ptree`'s Linux one, an extra supervising process per git call, which I've left out.

Fixed in c2104017f4: capture directories now carry a host tag and omp's pid, and every run sweeps this host's directories whose omp process is gone, on POSIX as well as on Windows. A run in progress is never touched however long it takes, since its omp is alive. Another host's or container's directories are left alone, since their pids mean nothing here. New test: of three leftover directories, the one of this host whose pid has exited is removed; one with a live pid and one of another host are kept. On the previous commit none is removed. Also checked on Windows. A background process that keeps writing to an already-deleted capture stays the case discussed in 4307969540.

Fixed in 13a6a41963: the fallback now calls a new `vcsGitHookLocation(dir, name, signal)` binding that discovers the repository and resolves the hook location together on the blocking pool, raced against the signal; `VcsGitRepo.hookLocation`, whose only caller this was, is gone. New test: with no git on `PATH` and the repository's config replaced by a named pipe, so the lookup's read stalls, the abort rejects with `AbortError`. With the previous synchronous discovery the test process hangs in that read and doesn't even react to SIGTERM. The no-git cases on Windows give the same results as before. The `runPostCheckoutHook` doc now also says that starting git (finding it on `PATH`, entering the worktree) still happens on the calling thread, since `Bun.spawn` offers no asynchronous start.

Fixed in c073e288da: on Linux the tag now also covers the boot id (`/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`) and the pid namespace (`/proc/self/ns/pid`), each read on its own so a missing one (no `/proc`, an AppArmor profile denying `boot_id`) doesn't drop the other. Containers with the same hostname and TMPDIR but their own pid namespaces therefore get different tags and never judge each other's directories. Unprivileged user namespaces are blocked on my machine, so I checked this with Docker instead of a unit test: two Ubuntu containers with the same hostname, user and TMPDIR volume. While one runs a hook probe (pid 38 in its namespace), the other's sweep deleted its live capture directory with the previous tag and leaves it alone now. The sweep test now takes this host's tag from a real run instead of recomputing it.

Not changed: this matches git. `git worktree add` runs `post-checkout` with stdin from `/dev/null` too (hook.c sets `no_stdin` unless `--to-stdin` is given). With git 2.53, a hook doing `read answer` gets an empty answer under `echo yes | git worktree add …`, and so does `git hook run`; only `git hook run --to-stdin=<file>` passes input. Passing the CLI's stdin through would therefore not reach the hook either way, and `omp worktree add` keeps parity with `git worktree add`. A hook that prompts can still use `/dev/tty`: the CLI doesn't detach the hook from the user's terminal, as the comment at that call says.

Fixed in 8bf7653cf6: the setup owner now also records the owning process's start time where the platform reports it (Linux: `starttime` from `/proc/<pid>/stat`; macOS: `pbi_start` via `proc_pidinfo`; read through a new `vcsProcessStartTime` binding over pi-builtins' existing process code). `isWorktreeSetupOwnerAlive` treats an owner as gone when its pid exists but now belongs to a process with a different start time, so `pr_checkout` takes over a worktree whose omp died even if the pid has since been reused. Owners without a start time (older marks, or Windows, where none is read) are still judged by the pid alone. Test: an owner naming this live process but with a different start time counts as gone; with the previous pid-only check it counted as alive.

Fixed in a8e79a89e7: the git probes (`git version`, `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/post-checkout`) no longer write to a capture file. They read stdout from a pipe, keep at most 4 KiB in memory, and stop at EOF, at that limit, or once git has exited and its line is complete (at most 100 ms after the exit otherwise); then the read end is closed. A background process the wrapper started that keeps writing gets a write error instead of filling a file, and the probe doesn't wait for it. Test: a `git` wrapper whose background process keeps writing to its inherited stdout; the hook still runs, and the writer exits once the probe closes the pipe. On the previous commit it kept writing into the unlinked capture file.

Fixed in f3d85fb6ad: each run now records its `git hook run` in its own file, `omp-setup-hook.<pid scope>-<pid>-<start>`, created exclusively and empty (the identity is in the name, so there is no rename to land late). Each run removes only its own file, and `worktreeSetupHookRunning` reports true while any recorded process is alive. Test: two runs with the same git dir; after the first one finishes, the second one's record still counts as running, and once both finish nothing does. On the previous commit the first run's cleanup removed the shared record.
